title: Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. (1 Cranch) 137 (1803) — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of the United States. Citation: 5 U.S. (1 Cranch) 137 (1803). Topic: judicial review. Educational digest: The Court held that it could not issue the requested writ because the statutory provision purporting to enlarge its original jurisdiction conflicted with the Constitution. The decision is widely associated with the US Supreme Court's authority to review the constitutionality of legislation. Verify the holding, procedural history and later doctrinal treatment in the official opinion and current constitutional law. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954) — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of the United States. Citation: 347 U.S. 483 (1954). Topic: equality and education. Educational digest: The Court held that racial segregation in public schools violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment; separate educational facilities are inherently unequal. Read the opinion and subsequent implementation decisions before applying the rule to a modern dispute. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966) — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of the United States. Citation: 384 U.S. 436 (1966). Topic: criminal procedure and custodial interrogation. Educational digest: The Court required procedural safeguards to protect the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination during custodial interrogation. The precise scope, exceptions and later interpretations must be checked against subsequent Supreme Court decisions and applicable state law. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges, 576 U.S. 644 (2015) — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of the United States. Citation: 576 U.S. 644 (2015). Topic: marriage equality and constitutional rights. Educational digest: The Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment requires states to license marriages between two people of the same sex and to recognize such marriages lawfully performed elsewhere. Consult the opinion and current subsequent law for precise application. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Donoghue v. Stevenson, [1932] AC 562 — case digest
text: Court: House of Lords (then the UK's highest appellate court). Citation: [1932] AC 562. Topic: negligence and duty of care. Educational digest: The decision is a foundational authority for the neighbour principle in negligence, explaining that a manufacturer may owe a duty of care to an ultimate consumer in appropriate circumstances. Modern duty-of-care analysis has developed through later cases and differs across jurisdictions. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: R v. Oakes, [1986] 1 SCR 103 — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of Canada. Citation: [1986] 1 SCR 103. Topic: Charter rights and proportionality. Educational digest: The Court developed the Oakes test for assessing whether a limit on a Charter right can be justified under section 1: pressing and substantial objective, rational connection, minimal impairment and proportionality of effects. Apply the current formulation and later refinements from official decisions. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Mabo v Queensland (No 2), (1992) 175 CLR 1 — case digest
text: Court: High Court of Australia. Citation: (1992) 175 CLR 1. Topic: native title and property law. Educational digest: The Court rejected the doctrine of terra nullius as a basis for denying pre-existing Indigenous land rights and recognised native title under Australian common law where the required connection and other legal criteria are established. Subsequent legislation and cases shape current claims. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225 — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of India. Citation: (1973) 4 SCC 225. Topic: constitutional amendment and basic structure. Educational digest: The Court held that Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 is wide but does not extend to destroying the Constitution's basic structure. The judgment contains multiple opinions; identify the relevant opinion and proposition before citing it. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, (1978) 1 SCC 248 — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of India. Citation: (1978) 1 SCC 248. Topic: personal liberty and procedural fairness. Educational digest: The decision interpreted Article 21 broadly and connected procedure depriving a person of life or personal liberty with fairness, justness and reasonableness, while reading Articles 14, 19 and 21 in an interconnected manner. Check the opinion and later constitutional developments for the precise rule. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, (1997) 6 SCC 241 — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of India. Citation: (1997) 6 SCC 241. Topic: workplace sexual harassment and fundamental rights. Educational digest: In the absence of enacted domestic legislation at the time, the Court laid down the Vishaka Guidelines to address workplace sexual harassment, drawing on constitutional guarantees and international obligations. Parliament later enacted the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013; use current statutory text and rules for present compliance. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 1 — case digest
text: Court: Supreme Court of India (nine-judge bench). Citation: (2017) 10 SCC 1. Topic: privacy and constitutional rights. Educational digest: The Court unanimously recognised privacy as a constitutionally protected fundamental right, grounded in liberty, dignity and other constitutional guarantees. The judgment contains concurring opinions; later cases address tests and application. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Naz Foundation v. Government of NCT of Delhi, 160 DLT 277 (2009) — High Court case digest
text: Court: Delhi High Court. Citation: 160 DLT 277 (2009). Topic: constitutional equality, privacy and criminal law. Educational digest: The Delhi High Court read down section 377 of the Indian Penal Code insofar as it criminalised consensual sexual acts between adults in private. Important subsequent history: the Supreme Court set aside this decision in Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013), and a Constitution Bench later invalidated the criminalisation of consensual same-sex relations between adults in Navtej Singh Johar (2018). The 2013 and 2018 Supreme Court decisions must be read before stating current law. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: S v. Makwanyane, 1995 (3) SA 391 (CC) — case digest
text: Court: Constitutional Court of South Africa. Citation: 1995 (3) SA 391 (CC). Topic: constitutional rights, dignity and punishment. Educational digest: The Court held the death penalty unconstitutional under the interim Constitution, emphasising dignity, life and freedom from cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment. Check the final Constitution and subsequent constitutional jurisprudence for current context. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Government of the Republic of South Africa v. Grootboom, 2001 (1) SA 46 (CC) — case digest
text: Court: Constitutional Court of South Africa. Citation: 2001 (1) SA 46 (CC). Topic: socio-economic rights and housing. Educational digest: The Court assessed the state's housing programme under the constitutional right of access to adequate housing and held that a reasonable programme must make provision for people in desperate need. The decision does not mean every individual has an immediately enforceable right to a particular house. Read the judgment and later cases. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Van Gend en Loos, Case 26/62, EU:C:1963:1 — case digest
text: Court: Court of Justice of the European Communities (now Court of Justice of the European Union). Case 26/62. Topic: EU law and direct effect. Educational digest: The Court held that the European Community constituted a new legal order and that qualifying provisions of Community law could confer rights on individuals enforceable before national courts. The doctrine's application depends on the legal instrument and later case law. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Handyside v. United Kingdom, App. no. 5493/72 — case digest
text: Court: European Court of Human Rights. Application no. 5493/72. Topic: freedom of expression. Educational digest: The Court explained that freedom of expression protects not only ideas favourably received but also those that offend, shock or disturb, subject to the Convention's permitted restrictions and the margin of appreciation. The precise proportionality analysis depends on facts and later jurisprudence. This digest is not the judgment text.

title: Economic change research framework — indicators and interpretation
text: Research framework, not a live data feed. For economic change, distinguish nominal from real GDP, headline from core inflation, unemployment from labour-force participation, policy rates from market rates, fiscal balance from public debt, and exchange-rate changes from purchasing-power changes. Always state country, reference period, unit, source, release date and revision status. Compare like-for-like series and explain uncertainty. World Bank, IMF, national statistical offices and central banks are primary places to obtain current data; do not invent current values.

title: Food, agriculture and food-shortage monitoring framework
text: Research framework, not a live shortage alert. Assess food availability, affordability, access, utilisation and stability. Distinguish local stockouts, market price spikes, acute food insecurity, chronic undernourishment and supply-chain disruption. Track crop production, export restrictions, input/fertiliser costs, weather, transport and household purchasing power. Use FAO food price and crop information, WFP situation reports, national food agencies and IPC/CH analyses where available. Record geography, date, affected population, commodity, severity and source. Do not infer a shortage from price movement alone.

title: Energy and critical-material shortage monitoring framework
text: Research framework, not a live shortage alert. For energy and critical materials, distinguish production shortfalls, low inventories, import dependence, price volatility, grid reliability, transport constraints and geopolitical/export controls. Track oil, gas, coal, electricity, refined products, critical minerals and fertiliser feedstocks separately. Use IEA statistics and reports, national energy regulators, grid operators, customs data and commodity agencies. State the time horizon and whether a risk is observed, forecast or scenario-based.

title: Global macroeconomic and financial stability monitoring framework
text: Research framework, not a live forecast. Monitor inflation, growth, public debt, balance of payments, reserves, exchange rates, financial conditions and sovereign risk. Separate observed official statistics from forecasts, projections and scenario analysis. Use IMF datasets and reports, World Bank indicators, BIS statistics and national central banks/statistical offices. Record publication date, data vintage, units, methodology and revisions. Do not turn a forecast into a statement of present fact.

title: Trade, logistics and supply-chain disruption monitoring framework
text: Research framework, not a live disruption feed. Analyse trade volumes, port congestion, shipping costs, route disruption, customs delays, export restrictions, input concentration and inventory buffers. Separate a temporary delivery delay from a sustained shortage. Use UNCTAD, WTO, national customs and statistics offices, port authorities and logistics agencies. Identify the affected product, region, supply-chain stage, observation date and confidence level. Avoid claims about current shortages unless supported by dated evidence.
